channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: SCOTUS: Postal Service can’t be sued for ‘intentional’ failure to deliver mail
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled the FTCA’s postal exception bars claims over intentional mail nondelivery, shielding USPS under sovereign immunity.

item.title: With witnesses, trust is key
item.description: Lawyers have to develop a bond with a witness in order to develop trust. Because without trust, we’re flying blind.

item.title: Are disparate impact discrimination claims still viable?
item.description: Recent action by the U.S. Department of Justice has created uncertainty regarding the status of disparate impact discrimination cases.

item.title: Financial services firm settles discrimination claim
item.description: The plaintiff was a middle-aged white woman who worked for a financial services firm. She had gender discrimination claims under Chapter 151B for failure to receive an internal promotion and also claims under the Massachusetts Equal Pay Act because she was not paid commensurately with some of her male colleagues.

item.title: Nursing home resident beaten by walker-wielding roommate
item.description: The plaintiff’s decedent, a resident of a nursing facility, was violently assaulted and killed by his roommate while lying in bed.

item.title: Lawsuit seeks compensation for deaths of Revere women at Belize resort
item.description: Families sue Royal Kahal Beach Resort and Navien over carbon monoxide deaths of three Revere women in Belize, alleging product defects and negligence.

item.title: Jeffrey Glassman Injury Lawyers Adopts Eve to Accelerate Its Shift to an AI-Native Practice
item.description: Jeffrey Glassman Injury Lawyers has partnered with leading legal AI platform Eve to transform into an AI-Native law firm. The collaboration brings AI into case development, intake, internal operations, and client communications—allowing attorneys and case managers to deliver stronger outcomes with greater speed, focus, and care.

item.title: Judge could limit mid-testimony consult with counsel, SCOTUS rules
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled a Texas judge did not violate the Sixth Amendment by limiting attorney discussions during a mid-testimony, overnight recess in a murder trial.

item.title: Judge: IRS broke law ‘approximately 42,695 times’ in giving DHS data
item.description: A federal judge ruled the IRS broke the law approximately 42,695 times by improperly sharing taxpayer addresses with DHS immigration officials in 2025.

item.title: New MCAD regulations facing pushback from bar
item.description: Employment lawyers and civil rights groups oppose MCAD procedural changes, citing online portal mandate and expanded dismissal powers.
